message: Hmm... which five-paragraph essay are we talking about? I am not a classicist, but Cicero's dispositio doesn't seem to have much in common with the creature I work with in freshman comp. That form -- introduction, three parallel points, and conclusion -- is a different, rhetorically weaker beast. I confess that I espouse disdain for the robotic 5-paragraph essay, yet in feshman comp class I reward students who can do it well -- that is, not robotically.
